Customer cares about latency SLOs for low-latency search summarization, cost per 1M tokens target, and private VPC deployment for PII-sensitive payloads. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-27 09:00 PT (recorded)
Duration: ~58m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ramirez (Redwood SE), Jun Park (Redwood Product), Priya Nair (Orion Edge Head of ML), James Hollis (Platform Eng), Elena Petrova (CTO), Samir Dutta (SRE)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
Redwood demo of model shortlist + bench plan. Discussed tradeoffs: latency vs cost, dedicated capacity vs hosted, private VPC needs, and a prioritized bench list.

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
00:04 Priya Nair: yes loud and clear, thanks Maya.
00:07 Maya Chen: awesome, quick intro — i'm Maya AE on the Redwood team, with Carlos our systems SE and Jun product. we'll run through the catalog shortlist workflow, show how we pick models to bench, and then a compatibility matrix view so you can see kernel/hw fit.
00:20 Elena Petrova: sounds good, we are mainly focused on search summarization latency, want under 250ms p50 if possible, and cost needs to be below our target — we gave a ballpark in the intake form.
00:33 Carlos Ramirez: great — we'll show the runtime profiling heuristics that map models to kernels and suggested quantization profiles. small note, some of the auto transcriptions later might say KV cash instead of cache, ignore that.
00:45 James Hollis: haha, good to know. also curious about VPC option for private payloads — do you have an on-prem path or strictly cloud vpc?
00:52 Maya Chen: we have both — Redwood Private with customer-managed control plane, and an on-prem package for air-gapped. for this demo we'll use the hosted console views but call out the mapping to Private.
01:05 Jun Park: jumping into the shortlist flow — here is a typical picklist: we start from graph filters (task type + latency target + token length distribution), then we run heuristics that score models by fit, cost, and stability.
01:25 Maya Chen: i'll share screen — apologies if screen flattens, let me know if folks can't see.
01:31 Priya Nair: seeing it. the shortlist has about a dozen open models, i see llama variants, mosaic, and a smaller distilled. how do you recommend prioritizing?
01:42 Carlos Ramirez: the playbook: 1) filter by token-length / context size — you sent example prompts that are around 128 tokens; 2) cost band — pick one low-cost quantized, one fp16-ish middle, one high-quality float; 3) runtime fit — if your p50 needs below 250ms we prefer models that map to cutlass kernels on our GPUs, or triton primitives depending on infra.
02:07 Samir Dutta: cutlass? you mean the CUDA CUTLASS libs? is that an implementation detail we need to think about?
02:13 Carlos Ramirez: yes, CUTLASS - it's part of the kernel selection. doesn't change the API surface, but impacts latency and we surface it in the compat matrix.
02:21 Maya Chen: here's an example bench prioritization card — shows expected p50, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens with an uncertainty band. note the numbers are landscape estimates until we run an in-house bench with your prompts.
02:38 James Hollis: can you walk through an example model row? say the open 13B quant variant — i want to see where it might fall.
02:45 Carlos Ramirez: sure — for the 13B quant we show: expected p50 ~220ms on an A10X-ish profile, tokens/sec ~350, cost estimate $120 per 1M tokens (with batching and KV cache savings that could lower it). caveat: quant profile may induce a small quality delta, we recommend running evals against your golden prompts.
03:10 Priya Nair: on quality delta — what's your workflow to detect regressions automatically? we can't manually inspect thousands of responses.
03:18 Jun Park: we have Redwood Optimize that ties quality monitoring to prompt sets/evals. you upload a small labeled set, we run auto-evals for drift/regression and alert on NPS-style drops. we can hook that into canary rollouts.
03:34 Elena Petrova: do you support function/tool-calling in the hosted API for structured output? our app relies on tools for entity extraction pipeline.
03:42 Maya Chen: yes, streaming and function calling are supported, and we preserve structured output across model variants. minor differences in tokenization can change token counts, we include that in cost estimates.
03:56 Samir Dutta: about VPC — our legal team wants to see KMS integration and audit logs, is that standard on Private?
04:05 Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM, SAML SSO, RBAC, and detailed audit logs. we'll attach the SOC2 summary and an HSM spec.
04:16 Priya Nair: thanks, please attach vendor SOC docs. that will speed procurement.
04:20 Maya Chen: noted.
04:24 Carlos Ramirez: back to benching — we'll suggest a minimal bench set: baseline prompts (N=50), adversarial edge cases (N=20), and generation diversity checks. bench runs will output latency percentiles, kernel mapping logs, and a compatibility flag if a model requires a different runtime path.
04:46 James Hollis: compatibility flag, meaning fallback to a variant?
04:49 Carlos Ramirez: exactly — if capacity or kernel mismatch occurs we recommend routing to a compatible quantized variant or a lower-cost region. Redwood's smart routing can fallback automatically.
05:00 Priya Nair: what about batch sizes — our throughput is bursty, typical concurrency is 40 qps peak with spikes.
05:07 Carlos Ramirez: we can show autoscaling policies for Dedicated and burst capacity for Hosted. batch sizes are workload-aware; small latency SLOs push us to tiny batch windows but KV cache helps a lot for repeated prefixes.
05:22 Priya Nair: KV cache — earlier you said KV cash on the initial note, haha.
05:26 Carlos Ramirez: yes transcription error — KV cache, sorry.
05:29 Jun Park: i'm going to flip to the compatibility matrix — this shows per-model which kernels and quant levels are supported on our runtime and which GPU families give best p50.
05:45 Elena Petrova: for our compliance team, can the matrix show where we need to enable encryption-at-rest for kv caches?
05:52 Carlos Ramirez: yes we annotate where sensitive caching is used and whether it's encrypted, we can toggle policies per route.
06:00 Maya Chen: demoing a bench result from a previous customer — not Orion — to give an example. note the bench uses your prompt length distribution, so numbers will change.
06:12 Priya Nair: are there any gotchas with quantization and named entity accuracy? in past we've seen subtle hallucinations with aggressive quant.
06:20 Carlos Ramirez: it's model-dependent. our bench includes diff checks against golden outputs and we produce per-token error metrics. recommended approach: run quantized models on non-critical paths first, compare F1/EM with the fp16 variant.
06:36 James Hollis: what's the timeline for a 2-week bench sprint? we want deliverables and checkpoints.
06:41 Maya Chen: typical sprint: week 1 — shortlist finalized, bench template filled, initial bench runs; week 2 — deeper evals, routing policy draft, and proposal for pilot. we'll have tri-weekly check-ins: kickoff, mid-sprint checkpoint, final review.
06:58 Priya Nair: ok that sounds good. can we ask you to prioritize models that are cheap but high chance of meeting latency? basically the low-hanging ones.
07:06 Carlos Ramirez: yes that's the low-cost quant + middle-tier fp16 approach. we'll provide expected upside from caching.
07:12 Jun Park: quick note on observability — Console shows token-level cost and route-level latency breakdowns, and we can export traces to your existing APM.
07:23 Samir Dutta: do you have Prometheus exporters? our infra wants metrics in Prom.
07:27 Carlos Ramirez: yes we export metrics and traces; we can provide a quick config snippet.
07:33 Elena Petrova: any legal concerns about open models — license scanning? we need to ensure permissive usage.
07:40 Maya Chen: we include a model catalog license field and we run license checks during onboarding; if a model has restrictive terms we'll flag it.
07:48 Priya Nair: good. also curious about cost modeling — can you show an example that accounts for batching, KV hit rate and tokenization variance?
07:56 Maya Chen: yes the bench template includes knobs: batch size distribution, KV hit rate, tokenization multiplier. we'll ask you to give us tokenization samples.
08:07 James Hollis: for the bench run logs you mentioned — what level of detail? raw latencies per-request or aggregated?
08:12 Carlos Ramirez: both — raw per-request with trace ids plus aggregated percentiles and histogram. we'll redact payloads if needed for privacy.
08:20 Priya Nair: perfect. what's the acceptance criteria post-bench for moving to pilot?
08:25 Maya Chen: typical acceptance: meets p50 latency target in 90% of traffic, no major quality regression on golden prompts, and cost within X% of target — we can define the X with you.
08:38 Elena Petrova: procurement will want pricing tiers for hosted vs dedicated — can you send a stub SOW for pilot pricing?
08:44 Maya Chen: yes we'll send pilot SOW + pricing bands.
08:46 Priya Nair: great, who owns the bench runs from your side?
08:49 Carlos Ramirez: Carlos + Maya to coordinate; James and Priya will provide prompt sets and a small sample of traffic.
08:58 Maya Chen: recap — we'll: 1) send shortlist + bench template (Maya) by Friday; 2) Carlos to run sample bench and share initial logs by June 2; 3) attach SOC2 and security docs; 4) schedule pilot kickoff next Tuesday 11am PT — any objections?
09:15 Priya Nair: no objections, sounds good.
09:19 Samir Dutta: quick question — competitors, we mentioned Anthropic earlier, curious how Redwood differs on runtime optimizations?
09:25 Carlos Ramirez: short answer: production-first runtime with kernel selection and workload-aware batching; we focus on predictable latency and cost levers. others focus more on model access.
09:39 Elena Petrova: thanks, closing thoughts?
09:42 Maya Chen: just that we'll try to keep the initial bench narrow and actionable; expect an email right after with attachments.
09:48 Priya Nair: thanks everyone, looking forward.
09:51 Meeting end.

Notes about transcript: speaker labels sometimes generic, minor transcription errors (e.g., KV cash), and some technical terms abbreviated.
notes: Customer emphasized latency p50 target and private deployment. Agreed to 2-week bench sprint and to share SOC2 + security details. Redwood to provide shortlist, bench template, and preliminary bench run logs.
